calls.head: The Canucks like Sasson’s line against Groulx’s
calls.body: At home, the Canucks keep sending Sasson’s line (Cotter, Sasson and Bains) out against opponents’ fourth lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Manny Malhotra keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Maple Leafs’ fourth line is Groulx, Sissons and Lettieri.

calls.body: The Maple Leafs’ power play is near the top of the league, and the Canucks’ kill is the worst. Every trip to the box hurts the Canucks more than most.

VAN.head: We gave Vancouver only a 37% chance, and it went the way we feared.

TOR.head: We gave Toronto a 63% chance, and they delivered.

surprises.head: Toronto brought the hits
surprises.body: Toronto usually hits less than most teams. Not tonight: a hit score of 141 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 81 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 25 games.

story.head: Blueger scores in his return to Vancouver
paras: William Nylander struck first for the Maple Leafs less than two minutes in, but Brock Boeser made it 1-1 for Vancouver on the power play midway through the first. Auston Matthews put the Leafs ahead for good early in the second. Zack MacEwen made it 3-1 midway through the period, and that one stood up as the winner. Max Sasson cut Toronto’s lead to 3-2 midway through the third. Teddy Blueger shut the door with an empty-netter with less than two minutes left, in his first game back in Vancouver.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Anthony Stolarz made 26 saves for the Maple Leafs, and Leevi Meriläinen stopped 24 of 27 at the other end. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Dakota Joshua, even without a point, by our Swing measure.

The Canucks killed off a two-man advantage that lasted just over a minute midway through the first. The Maple Leafs improved to 8-6-2, sixth in the Atlantic, while the Canucks dropped to 3-12-1, still last in the NHL.

items.text: Jack Roslovic has a point in six straight games.
The Canucks have lost five straight at home.

The Maple Leafs won without Kirill Marchenko, Nick Blankenburg, John Tavares and others. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Islanders were missing more at the time.
Elias Pettersson (#40)’s six-game point streak ended.
